clue.text: Polish bishop recalled cross American with clock

definitions.note: a noun here: a substance used to polish wood

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the string runs back the other way

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
standard abbreviation
W is short for with
to clock someone is informally to notice or see them

explanation.surface: A Polish bishop remembers an angry American who came with a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality; it is the material you polish with. 'Clock' is slang for notice, and only the pieces after the bishop are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is the wax bees make, commonly rubbed into furniture as a wood polish.

clue.text: Sweeper losing male child's piece of jewellery

indicators.note: something that is lost is no longer there, so a letter drops out

parts.note: a broom sweeps the floor
M is the abbreviation for male; it is taken away
CH is the dictionary abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A cleaner or broom somehow loses a boy's bit of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeper' could be a football position or a cleaner; here it is the tool itself. The 's is short for 'has', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornamental pin fastened to clothing, a standard item of jewellery.

clue.text: Catch ten cycling with artist quietly

indicators.note: going round a cycle moves the front letter round to the back

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone catches ten people cycling alongside a painter who rides quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN sends its first letter to the back to become ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to snare or capture by trickery, a verb meaning much the same as catch.

clue.text: Comic sketch framed by husband Al in retreat

indicators.note: a picture framed by something has it running all round its edges

parts.note: a wit is a comic person
to sketch is to draw
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch is performed by a husband named Al while he is away on retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic sketch' reads as one thing, a funny sketch; split it into two separate pieces, with the frame applying only to the sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal is a pulling back of troops, the same military sense as a retreat.

clue.text: Gas flame previously turned on after noon

indicators.note: something turned round faces the opposite way

parts.note: a former lover is an old flame, an ex
N is the abbreviation for noon
taken as written, placed after the N

explanation.surface: The gas flame was switched on earlier, some time after midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas flame' looks like one object, but 'flame previously' is the ex. 'after' just places ON behind N.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is one of the noble gases, the inert elements found in trace amounts in air.

clue.text: Stuffed eating starters of such in Italy?

definitions.text: Stuffed eating starters of such in Italy?

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside itself

parts.note: stuffed after a big meal means full

indicators.note: starters come first, so only the opening letters are wanted

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone feels full after eating dishes like this while in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: FULL takes in SI, then I for Italy ends it. The whole clue also describes the answer: a pasta that stuffs Italian diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusilli are spiral pasta shapes, exactly the sort of food you would eat until stuffed in Italy.

clue.text: Daydream of naked miser following drinks

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece is placed second

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy drink

indicators.note: someone naked has nothing on the outside, so the outer letters are stripped

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A daydream about a stingy person with no clothes, after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following drinks' puts the stripped miser after the soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise is to indulge in pleasant imaginings, which is what a daydreamer does.

clue.text: Bars maybe removing old drains
Lacy clothes perhaps hang on centre of frieze

parts.note: to hang on is to stay around, to linger

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two letters in the middle of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: Lace garments are hung up somewhere near the middle of a decorative frieze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang on' here means wait around, not suspend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, often made of lace, so lacy clothes are an example.

clue.text: Bladed item from new Ikea set inscribed by Charlie

indicators.note: a word inscribed by something has that thing written inside it
something made new is rearranged into a different form

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sharp item comes from a new flat-pack Ikea set with Charlie's name engraved on it.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into the letters of IKEA SET, and the lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skate is a boot fitted with a metal blade for gliding over ice.

clue.text: Group of players periodically scrubbed low-cut vests

indicators.note: wiping out letters at regular intervals leaves every other one

parts.note: the even-placed letters remain once the others are removed

explanation.surface: A band of musicians keeps scrubbing their skimpy low-cut vests.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first, third, fifth letters and so on of 'low-cut vests', ignoring the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight musicians performing together.

clue.text: French city north-east writer visits for a bit once

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
compass abbreviation
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer from the north-east pays a short visit to a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' here is a coin, as in a threepenny bit, and 'once' says the coin belongs to the days before decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: Before decimal currency Britain had small coins called bits, and ninepence was a sum such a coin could represent.

clue.text: Spanish nobleman tucks into fish with no white wine

indicators.note: to tuck into a space is to slide inside it

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
Don is a Spanish title of rank
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A Spanish grandee tucks into a fish supper with no white wine to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but it places the nobleman between the fish and the refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a green grape variety and the dry white wine made from it.

clue.text: Vegetable from part of Hull sent back

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came

parts.note: the keel is the lowest part of a ship's hull

explanation.surface: Vegetables from one district of Hull are returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hull the Yorkshire port; the part is a boat's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A leek is an onion-family plant grown for its long edible stem.

clue.text: Delivery of office supplies going nowhere

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is how the words are said out loud

parts.note: paper, envelopes and pens are stationery, spelt with an E

explanation.surface: A shipment of office supplies is stuck and not moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' looks like a parcel arriving; it means the way something is spoken. The two spellings sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary is not moving at all, which is exactly going nowhere.

clue.text: Dalek struggling with one harsh hilly region

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, its parts thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one
harsh rules are strict

explanation.surface: A Dalek has a hard time on steep terrain, famously unable to manage hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Only DALEK is rearranged. Daleks are the robot villains of Doctor Who; the Lake District is a mountainous national park in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District is England's most mountainous area, full of fells, so it is a hilly region.

clue.text: Survival in close university contest Newton enters

indicators.note: whoever enters a thing goes inside it

parts.note: the close of something is its end
standard abbreviation
a race is a contest
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton takes part in a tight university competition and just about survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the noun, an ending, not the adjective for a tight contest. N goes into RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to last out hardship, which is what survival amounts to.

clue.text: Seafood option rascal lopsidedly carries

indicators.note: what carries something holds it within itself

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A scoundrel staggers along unevenly carrying a seafood order.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'raSCAL LOPSidedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are shellfish commonly served in restaurants, one choice from a seafood menu.

clue.text: English fruit mainly served up with dry eastern dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from the bottom
mainly means most but not all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a lemon is a citrus fruit; its final letter goes
TT means teetotal, so someone who is dry
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An English fruit dish is mostly served with a dry Eastern dish.
explanation.walkthrough: E and LEMO together turn round to give OMELE. 'Dry' means not drinking alcohol here.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a cooked egg preparation, one of the most familiar simple dishes.

clue.text: Remarks about staff initially defying orders from above

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: remarks are comments
to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: initially points to the very first letter only

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Remarks about staff first defying instructions from senior management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders from above' reads as instructions from bosses, but it means divine law handed down from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments are rules said to be handed down by God, orders from heaven.

clue.text: Stubborn Remainer allowed to host current politician

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house

parts.note: allowed means let
I is the symbol for electric current
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A die-hard Remain voter is given room to entertain the current politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-R 'Remainer' evokes someone who voted to stay in the EU at Brexit; here it just means something that stays put. I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that clings to rocks, and figuratively a person who refuses to leave.

clue.text: What's kept by retired vinicultural lecturers?

definitions.text: What's kept by retired vinicultural lecturers?

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the letters go in reverse
what is kept by something is held inside it

parts.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: What do former wine-growing academics keep in store?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in 'viniculturAL LECturers', read upwards. The whole clue doubles as a description: wine experts keep a store of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is also a person's stock of wine, just what retired wine experts would keep.

clue.text: Blur essentially copied singer

indicators.note: a copy is a duplicate, so the piece appears twice over
the essence of something is at its heart, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
the same central pair again, as a copy

explanation.surface: The band Blur basically imitated another pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British rock band, which makes the surface feel musical. Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous since the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is the stage name of a long-running Scottish pop vocalist, so she is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Minor leapt around back garden construction?

indicators.note: letters thrown around end up in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child jumped about on some structure in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: the answer is one thing you might build out the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung frame often set up behind a family home for children to bounce on.

clue.text: Female servants bringing down article for king

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing the article A down moves it lower, further along the word

parts.note: maids are female servants; the article A in that word is moved two places down

explanation.surface: Maidservants bring a piece of writing down to the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In MAIDS the A slides two places lower to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: One of seven miners in a film uncovered bottom

indicators.note: with its cover off, the outer layer is gone, leaving the inside letters

parts.words: One of seven miners in a film
parts.note: Grumpy, one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White, who work in a mine; drop its ends

explanation.surface: A dwarf from the Snow White film shows his bare behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miners' is fair because Disney's dwarfs dig in a diamond mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters of an animal, and informally a person's bottom.

clue.text: Beaten outside of unit within horrid dungeon

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits in the other
something horrid is a mess, its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outside of something is its edges, so just the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A defeated army unit is shut away inside a nasty dungeon.
explanation.walkthrough: The edge letters go inside first, and only then is the whole nine-letter string rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outgunned is to be overpowered by a stronger opponent, so defeated or beaten.

clue.text: Shock from circuit father brought back

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so read backwards

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An electric shock from a faulty circuit, with Dad brought back round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' and 'circuit' suggest electricity, but the circuit is a lap of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay someone, a verb meaning to shock.

clue.text: Tower piano protected by metal base

indicators.note: what is protected by something is shielded all round by it

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A tall tower has a piano kept safe on a metal base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal base' looks like one phrase; split it. P goes inside STEEL, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall pointed tower of a church.

clue.text: Shady character is unforthcoming and austere, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: someone shy is unforthcoming
an austere manner is stern; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A shady character keeps quiet and has a severe manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a straight character sketch; 'and' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest operator, especially a crooked lawyer, a disreputable person.
